answer:
Confirmed — there's no campaign/session delete route on the worker side at all.

**Login:** Entirely client-side, no password/backend call. `AuthService.login(username)` (`frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts`) looks up `localStorage` key `ai_dnd_user_<username.toLowerCase()>`; if found, loads that `UserProfile`, else creates a fresh one (`{username, campaigns: []}`) and persists it. `LoginComponent.login()` just calls this and routes to `/characters` or shows the campaign list.

**Campaigns:** Stored only in browser `localStorage` as `UserProfile.campaigns: CampaignSlot[]`, under keys `ai_dnd_user` (current user) and `ai_dnd_user_<username>` (per-user). Each `CampaignSlot` holds `sessionId`/`characterId` pointers into the backend, not the game data itself. Real game state lives server-side: character rows in D1 (`worker/migrations/0001_initial_schema.sql`) and session state in KV (`worker/src/services/session.ts`, key `session:<id>`, 7-day TTL via `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`).

**Deleting a campaign slot:** `LoginComponent.deleteCampaign()` → `AuthService.removeCampaign(slotId)` only filters the slot out of the local `campaigns` array and re-persists to `localStorage` — it never calls the API (`GameApiService` has no delete-campaign/character method, and `worker/src/routes` has no campaign/session delete route). So the server-side character (D1) and session (KV) are **not deleted**; they become orphaned and the KV session simply expires naturally after 7 days (`SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`), while the D1 character row persists indefinitely.
